questions.stem: Television broadcasting began in Australia in 1956, just in time for which event?
options: The coronation of Elizabeth II
The first Moon landing
The Melbourne Olympic Games
The Sydney Olympic Games
questions.explanation: Sydney's first station went to air in September 1956 and Melbourne's soon after, ahead of the Melbourne Olympics in November. The coronation was in 1953, before Australian television existed, the Moon landing was in 1969, and Sydney hosted the Olympics in 2000.

questions.stem: Which development in the 1950s best shows growing American influence on young Australians?
options: A revival of bush ballads by writers such as Henry Lawson
Rock 'n' roll records, films and touring acts from the US
The arrival of the Beatles and the British 'Mersey sound' on tour
Radio serials and comedy programs made by the BBC
questions.explanation: Bill Haley and the Comets toured in 1957, American films and records reached Australian teenagers, and local singers copied the new style. The Beatles were a British influence of the mid-1960s, and Lawson's ballads date from the 1890s.

questions.stem: Johnny O'Keefe, known as 'The Wild One', is significant in Australian popular culture as:
options: the first presenter of the music television show Countdown
one of Australia's first home-grown rock 'n' roll stars
the American singer whose 1957 tour began rock in Australia
the lead singer of the band Yothu Yindi in the 1990s
questions.explanation: O'Keefe had hits from 1958 and hosted the ABC's Six O'Clock Rock, showing that Australians could make rock 'n' roll, not just listen to American imports. The 1957 American tour was by Bill Haley, and Countdown began in 1974, long after O'Keefe's first hits.

questions.stem: Why did the post-war baby boom change Australian popular culture by the 1960s?
options: Families had less money to spend on leisure than during the Depression
Young people were banned from watching any television until they turned 18
Most teenagers left school at twelve and had no time for entertainment
A large teenage generation became a market for music, fashion and films
questions.explanation: The high birth rate after 1945, together with migration and the long boom, produced millions of young people with more spending money and longer schooling than earlier generations. Businesses aimed records, clothes, films and magazines at them, and a distinct youth culture emerged.

questions.stem: The Beatles toured Australia in June 1964 and drew enormous crowds. What did this show about popular culture at the time?
options: Most young Australians preferred classical music to pop
British pop had joined American music in shaping youth culture
Australians had stopped listening to any overseas music at all by then
Rock music had been banned in Australia until that year
questions.explanation: Beatlemania showed that the 'British invasion' had added to, rather than replaced, the American influence of the 1950s, and that young people were now a powerful audience. Rock 'n' roll had been popular since the 1950s, so it was not newly allowed in 1964.

questions.stem: The 1959 film On the Beach, shot in Melbourne, showed the last survivors of a nuclear war waiting for deadly radiation to reach them. Which historical context does it reflect?
options: Excitement about the 1956 Olympic Games in Melbourne
Cold War fear of a nuclear war between the superpowers
Wartime memories of the Japanese bombing of Darwin in 1942
Concern about bushfires in south-eastern Australia
questions.explanation: The film, based on Nevil Shute's novel, appeared during the nuclear arms race between the United States and the Soviet Union, when people feared atomic war could end civilisation. Popular culture of the 1950s and 1960s often reflected these fears, alongside spy films and fallout shelters.

questions.stem: Why did Australian governments fund film-making from the early 1970s, leading to films such as Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975)?
options: Because cinemas had been closed by law after television arrived
Because Hollywood studios had stopped sending any films to Australia
To make training films for the Australian armed forces in Vietnam
To tell Australian stories on screen instead of relying on Hollywood
questions.explanation: Few Australian feature films were made in the 1950s and 1960s, so governments set up bodies such as the Australian Film Development Corporation and the Australian Film Commission. The revival produced films including Picnic at Hanging Rock, Mad Max and Gallipoli. Hollywood films kept arriving, which is why local funding was felt to be needed.

questions.stem: Which 1986 Australian film became a worldwide box-office hit and boosted overseas tourism to Australia?
options: Gallipoli
Crocodile Dundee
Mad Max
Picnic at Hanging Rock
questions.explanation: Crocodile Dundee, starring Paul Hogan, was hugely successful in the United States and helped sell an outback image of Australia to tourists. Mad Max (1979), Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975) and Gallipoli (1981) were earlier films of the revival.

questions.stem: Countdown (1974–87) on ABC television mattered to Australian music because it:
options: played only classical and jazz music, not rock or pop
was taken off air after one season for playing rock music
gave Australian bands national exposure beside overseas acts
was the first program ever broadcast on Australian television
questions.explanation: Each week the show reached a national audience, helping launch or boost acts such as AC/DC, Skyhooks and INXS. Australian television had begun in 1956, almost twenty years earlier.

questions.stem: Which Australian TV soap opera became hugely popular in Britain in the late 1980s and helped launch Kylie Minogue's career?
options: Skippy
Neighbours
Home and Away
Countdown
questions.explanation: Minogue played Charlene in Neighbours before her first hit single in 1987, and the show drew huge audiences in Britain. Home and Away was also exported but did not feature her, Countdown was a music program, and Skippy was a 1960s children's series.

questions.stem: Why is Australia II's win in the 1983 America's Cup often linked to national identity?
options: It was the very first sporting event shown live on Australian television
It was won by a crew made up entirely of First Nations sailors
It ended 132 years of American victories and set off national celebrations
It was Australia's first gold medal at any Olympic Games
questions.explanation: The New York Yacht Club had held the Cup since 1851, so Australia II's win was a famous upset, and Prime Minister Bob Hawke joked that no boss should sack a worker for missing work to celebrate. Australia had won Olympic gold as early as 1896, and television had begun in 1956.

questions.stem: At the 2000 Sydney Olympics, why was Cathy Freeman's 400 metres win so significant?
options: It was the only gold medal that Australia won at the whole of the Sydney Olympic Games
She became the first Australian ever to win an Olympic medal of any kind
She won the race at the 1956 Melbourne Games as well as in 2000
An Aboriginal athlete who had lit the Olympic flame won gold before a home crowd
questions.explanation: Freeman lit the cauldron at the opening ceremony and then won the final, and many people saw her victory as a symbol of reconciliation. Australia won many gold medals in Sydney, and Australians had been winning Olympic medals since 1896.

questions.stem: Yothu Yindi's 1991 hit 'Treaty' combined Yolŋu song and dance with rock and dance music. What was its message?
options: A call for the treaty Bob Hawke had promised in 1988
A celebration of the Federation of Australia in 1901
A protest against Australia's role in the Vietnam War
An advertising song for tourism in the Northern Territory
questions.explanation: Hawke had said at Barunga in 1988 that a treaty would be made, but none followed, and the song pointed to the broken promise. Its success in the charts brought a First Nations political message into mainstream popular culture.

questions.stem: In the 2000s, which change transformed how many Australians bought and listened to music?
options: Colour television replaced black-and-white
Downloads and streaming replaced CDs
Cassette tapes replaced vinyl records
Radio broadcasting began for the first time
questions.explanation: MP3 players, online stores and later streaming services moved music from physical discs to digital files, changing how artists earned money. Cassettes spread in the 1970s and 1980s, Australian radio began in 1923, and colour television arrived in 1975.

questions.stem: Critics in the 1950s and 1960s warned that Australian culture was being 'Americanised'. Which evidence would best support a historian arguing it was not simply Americanised?
options: Most television programs shown in Australia in the 1960s were made in the United States
American rock 'n' roll records topped Australian charts in the late 1950s
Hollywood films filled the programs of most Australian cinemas
Rules required commercial TV stations to show set amounts of Australian programs
questions.explanation: Local content rules, introduced in the early 1960s and strengthened after campaigns such as 'TV: Make it Australian' in 1970, show Australians actively protecting their own culture. The other three facts are real, but they are evidence for Americanisation, not against it.
